report.source_text: we took him to OR and we did bicoronal skin incision and bifrontal craniotomy done, then extradural DE vascularization of the tumor and dissection plane created between the tumor and frontal lobes, then tumor debulked centrally with suction for the suckable part and with microsissor for the non suckable portion, complete tumor excision achieved and optic nerve, optic chiasm, ICA, pituitary infundibulum identified and protected from any iatrogenic injury(see Fig. 3), patient extubated and transferred smoothly with GCS 15/15,behavioral change was the same as the preoperative baseline on first 3 days then completely resolved on the 6th day, vision on the left side then he can count from 2 m, anosmia remain the same as the preoperative state, no epistaxis, nasal obstruction improved with no night snoring.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old Black African male presented with a one-year history of progressive nasal obstruction, anosmia, epistaxis, and headache, followed by recent left-sided visual loss and cognitive changes. MRI and CT imaging on admission revealed a T1 hypointense, T2 hyperintense anterior cranial fossa lesion arising from the left ethmoid and sphenoid sinuses, compressing left optic structures and explaining the visual loss. Preoperative biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma with mucinous differentiation (variable-sized glands lined by columnar cells with apical mucinous cytoplasm in desmoplastic stroma), specifically identified as sinonasal intestinal mucinous type adenocarcinoma. Bifrontal craniotomy with complete tumor excision was performed with successful protection of critical structures (optic nerve, optic chiasm, ICA, pituitary infundibulum). Postoperative course showed resolution of behavioral changes by day 6, improvement in left-sided vision (counting from 2 m), and improvement in nasal obstruction and snoring, though anosmia persisted.
